CHIEF COMPLAINT
Yearly exam

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Patient is a 24-year-old female with a history of type 2 diabetes and hypertension presenting for her yearly physical examination. She reports that she has been doing well overall but began working in a bakery this summer. She notes that her proximity to desserts and treats at work has led to increased snacking and consumption of sweets during her shifts. She reports her blood sugars have been up and down, which she attributes to her diet. She confirms she has been taking her diabetes medication as prescribed without any missed doses. She acknowledges that resisting the temptation of desserts at work has been challenging. Regarding her hypertension, she reports her blood pressure has been good despite the fluctuations in her diabetes levels. She denies any safety concerns.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Patient denies any additional concerns. Reports sleeping well with a full eight hours of sleep per night.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Type 2 diabetes mellitus
Hypertension
Systolic ejection murmur (grade 2, unchanged from prior)

MEDICATIONS
Metformin twice daily
Lisinopril 10 mg once daily

ALLERGIES
Not discussed.

FAMILY HISTORY
Not discussed.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Patient works in a bakery since summer.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
General: Normal exam
Cardiovascular: Heart regular rate and rhythm; grade 2 systolic ejection murmur noted, unchanged from prior
Pulses: Good bilaterally
Carotid: No bruits
Neck: No thyromegaly
Extremities: No edema; grips equal bilaterally
Neurologic: Intact; able to feel touch; motor function intact
Lungs: Clear bilaterally

RESULTS
Hemoglobin A1c: Elevated
Blood pressure: Good, within normal limits
Vital signs: Normal

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
1. Type 2 diabetes mellitus - out of control. Hemoglobin A1c elevated; goal is under 7%, preferably under 6%. No medication changes at this time as this appears diet-related. Patient instructed to cut down on snacking and additional sweets. Patient to check fasting blood sugars in the morning and call results in two weeks. Follow-up visit in approximately two months to reassess. If not improved, will consider adding additional medication.

2. Hypertension - relatively stable. Continue current medication (lisinopril 10 mg once daily). No changes at this time.
